output.brief: Turnaround doubled mainly because of the 1 April change to settlement authority. Adjusters' limit was cut from $10,000 to $2,500 after an audit found overpayments. Claims of $2,500–$10,000 (about 53% of closures) now need a team-lead approval. Those claims wait about 16 days for sign-off, up from 0.7. Their total time rose from 10.4 to 26 days. Other stages are almost unchanged, including investigation and document indexing, and claims under $2,500 and over $10,000 are unchanged. The three team leads went from about 38 to over 200 items a week. They approve about 199 a week, and the backlog keeps growing, from 11 to 455. The change record shows no workload assessment was done. The hail surge, the loss of two senior adjusters and the Quillfast switch don't explain the pattern. New claims and staffing were back to normal by June. Contract adjusters and a return to the old imaging provider would not fix the bottleneck. Don't sign either yet. Don't discipline the team leads. Don't drop the control unilaterally. Work with Internal Audit to add approval capacity for that band, for example by certifying senior adjusters as second approvers. Keep a second review on every claim in the band. Track time pending approval weekly. Wait for the December re-test before setting permanent thresholds. Whether the control actually reduces overpayments is still unmeasured. I'm confident in the main finding.
